{{Short description|American statistician (1925–2004)}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=October 2025}}
{{use mdy dates|date=October 2025}}
[[File:I._Richard_Savage_(October_1966).jpg|thumb|right|I. Richard Savage in 1966]]
'''I. Richard Savage''' (October 26, 1925 – June 4, 2004{{r|Sampson1999}}) was an American statistician who specialized in [[Census|population censuses]]. He was [[Emeritus|professor emeritus]] and former chair of statistics at [[Yale University]].  He was an elected fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].

==Education==
Savage earned his BS from the [[University of Chicago]] and his MSc from the [[University of Michigan]].{{r|YaleBulletin2004}} He earned a PhD in statistics from [[Columbia University]] in 1954 where he studied under the tutelage of [[Howard Levene]]. His thesis was titled: ''Contributions to the Theory of Rank Order Statistics.''{{r|MathGenealogy}} His early research continued his work on [[nonparametric statistics]], especially [[Ranking (statistics)|rank order statistics]].{{r|YaleBulletin2004}}

==Career==
Savage's first position after completing his PhD was as a mathematical statistician at the National Bureau of Standards (now the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]]), where he published his PhD thesis.{{r|Sampson1999}}{{sfn|Savage|1954}} He then had a number of university faculty positions, including [[Stanford University]], [[Harvard Business School]], [[Imperial College London]], [[University of Minnesota]], and [[Florida State University]].{{r|YaleBulletin2004}} In 1974, he joined the Department of Statistics at Yale University where he stayed until his retirement in 1990. He was chair of the department from 1976 to 1978.{{r|Sampson1999}}

==Recognition and service==
Savage was elected a fellow of the [[List of fellows of the American Statistical Association|American Statistical Association]], the [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science|American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]. He was co-editor of both the [[Journal of the American Statistical Association]] and the [[Annals of Statistics]]. In 1984, he was [[List of presidents of the American Statistical Association|president of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|Sampson1999|YaleBulletin2004}} In 1993, he was presented with the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award]].{{r|ASAFoundersAward}}

==Personal life==
While studying for his PhD, Savage met JoAnn Osherow. They married in 1950 and had two daughters.{{r|Sampson1999}} Savage was the brother of [[Leonard Jimmie Savage]].{{r|Sampson1999}}

Savage contracted [[polio]] in 1945 that left him legally blind and needing the use of a wheelchair.{{r|Sampson1999}} He died from [[post-polio syndrome]] in 2004. He was 78 years old.{{r|YaleBulletin2004|AANObit2004}}
